q: Why does the random-mixed-state ensemble (Haar purification of a 16-dim state) empirically top out at C ~= 0.65 in 1000 samples despite C <= 1 being allowed? Is the induced measure on 2-qubit density matrices heavily concentrated below the boundary of allowed concurrence, and how does the concentration depend on ancilla dimension?
basis: In our 1000-sample sweep C_max = 0.6515 and E_max = 0.5313 — both well below the algebraic bound of 1. This suggests a measure-concentration phenomenon we did not predict from the paper.
next_steps: (a) Repeat with ancilla dim 4, 8, 16, 32; plot the 99th-percentile C. (b) Compare against known analytic marginals of the Hilbert-Schmidt vs Bures induced measures. (c) Check whether the concentration curve matches Zyczkowski-Sommers predictions for random 2-qubit states.

q: How many random HJW decompositions are needed before the empirical minimum average pure-state entanglement converges to the Wootters E_F within 10^-3, and is this rate universal across the space of 2-qubit density matrices?
basis: For the Bell-diagonal state 0.7|Phi+><Phi+| + 0.3|Psi-><Psi-| we needed 400 samples to reach 0.289 vs Wootters 0.250 — a 15% gap that we did not close by brute force alone.
next_steps: (a) Sweep decomposition count 10^1 - 10^6 for a fixed state and plot convergence. (b) Repeat for high-C vs low-C states. (c) Add gradient-based ensemble optimization (parameterize U on U(K)) and compare wall-clock to reach the same tolerance.

q: The Wootters closed form is unique to two qubits. For two-qutrit states, do variational lower bounds (e.g. SDP-relaxations of the convex-roof extension) empirically agree with Wootters when the qutrit is projected onto a qubit subspace, and can they be extended to give tight closed forms in special families (e.g. isotropic qutrit states)?
basis: The Wootters proof relies on a magic basis + spin-flip structure that is intrinsic to SU(2) x SU(2). We had no way to check higher-dim generalizations in this replication.
next_steps: (a) Implement the Terhal-Vollbrecht formula for isotropic states and cross-check on qutrit-projected qubits. (b) Numerically compare SDP lower bounds (via pypsd / cvxpy) to Wootters on qubit sub-states embedded in a qutrit.

q: For 'Werner-like' states rho(p) = p |psi><psi| + (1-p) I/d with an arbitrary entangled |psi> (not Bell), does the separability threshold move to p_c = 1 / (1 + d * |<psi|Bell>|^2) or a different closed form, and does Wootters' formula still give the exact E_F in that generalization?
basis: Our sweep confirmed the p_c = 1/3 kink for |psi> = |Phi+>, but we did not test other entangled pure states of two qubits.
next_steps: (a) Sample 20 random pure two-qubit states, form their p-mixtures with I/4, and find the separability threshold p_c(psi) numerically. (b) Fit against candidate closed forms; report which one matches to machine precision.

q: Our HJW-brute-force gives upper bounds on E_F that converge from above. Is there a similarly cheap constructive procedure that converges from below (e.g. via dual SDP or entanglement-witness maximization), giving two-sided numerical bounds — and if so, does the gap close at the same rate as the upper bound?
basis: We only had one-sided evidence that E_F <= 0.289; without a lower bound the brute-force test cannot certify E_F = 0.250 by itself.
next_steps: (a) Implement the standard entanglement-witness LP for two-qubit states and read off the lower bound. (b) Compare wall-clock and convergence to the upper-bound HJW sampler on the same 100-state benchmark. (c) Report gap = UB - LB vs number of samples.
